questions: Did progress hold at or above 0.155 on the s-bend and 0.107 on the slalom, compared with iteration 5?
Did max_error stay at or below 0.069 on every track? If it rose, at what progress does the robot now leave the track?
Did steering_oscillation fall with the wider track (lower turn rate per unit of PWM difference), or did it stay in the 0.07 to 0.15 range?
Does the wider track change the s-bend progress in the direction predicted (up) or does it lower progress as the narrow track did in iteration 3?
If any run finishes, what is the completion_time, and is it still limited by speed or by the controller?

intent: Revert mass to 0.6 kg, which scored best in iteration 5, and keep wheel_radius 0.035 m and the sensor layout. Change only wheel_track, from 0.12 to 0.14 m, to test whether a wider track lowers turn-rate overshoot at the higher ground speed. Expected result: progress holds at or above 0.155 on the s-bend and 0.107 on the slalom, and max_error stays at or below 0.069 on all tracks.
learning: Iteration 6 showed mass 0.5 kg lowers progress and raises max_error at wheel_radius 0.035 m, so mass is not the lever at this speed. Speed (wheel_radius) is a real lever, and the iteration 5 mass of 0.6 kg is the baseline. If the wider track lifts progress with max_error held, the next step is to test wheel_track 0.16 m. If it lowers progress as the narrow track did, turn rate is not the limit and the next test is wheel_radius 0.04 m with the 0.6 kg mass.
rationale: Iteration 6 (mass 0.5 kg, wheel_radius 0.035 m) scored 49.76, below iteration 5 (51.01). Progress fell on the s-bend (0.155 to 0.149) and slalom (0.107 to 0.103), and max_error rose on the s-bend (0.065 to 0.068). The oval was unchanged at progress 0.11 and max_error 0.0616. Lower mass did not help, and the extra drift shows the robot is now correcting less well at speed. This matches the Integrator's rule for the case where progress does not rise and max_error grows: return mass to 0.6 kg and keep wheel_radius 0.035 m, which is the best-scoring state so far. Steering oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.15), so the robot drifts steadily rather than jittering. Across iterations 0 to 6, span, footprint, lead and body/track changes each left max_error almost unchanged. Only the wheel radius increase (iteration 5) raised progress without pushing max_error past the 0.069 band. The next untested lever is turn-rate-per-PWM through wheel_track. Iteration 3 narrowed the track to 0.10 m and lowered s-bend progress, so this iteration widens it to 0.14 m, the opposite test. A wider track lowers turn rate for the same wheel difference, which may reduce overshoot at speed. I expect progress to stay near 0.155 on the s-bend, with max_error at or below 0.069. If progress falls again or max_error exceeds 0.069, I will return the track to 0.12 m.
